SEBoK Competency Assessment, Distilled

*Fourth-batch SEBoK distillation, batch 5 doc 6. Target article 404'd; competency assessment is carried by ENG Competency Model, Competency (glossary), Assessing Individuals, Roles and Competencies (SE-033), Team Capability, Enabling Individuals (knowledge area), Technical Leadership in SE, Enterprise Capability Management. Dispersed-instrument pattern at moderate density (eight carriers). The discipline composes two co-located lattices: competency dimensions (SE-033 universal-sibling: technical, professional, leadership) × proficiency levels (ordinal: awareness, supervised practitioner, practitioner, lead practitioner, expert) — two-axis universal-sibling (SE-039 §VII.6 candidate from SE-082). Proficiency-level ordinal is Doc 572 Appendix D.5. Multi-scope assessment (individual / team / enterprise) is Cluster B three-scale sub-form (SE-115). Six corpus forms compose; two-axis universal-sibling instance strengthens formalization candidate.*

II. Source Read

The target page does not exist as standalone. Competency assessment is dispersed across eight host articles spanning the Enabling Individuals knowledge area (Part 5). Carriers: ENG Competency Model carries the DoD framework as exemplar; Competency glossary defines the term and references assessment tools; Assessing Individuals focuses on evaluating competency needs and tailoring competency models to organizational context; Roles and Competencies (SE-033) carries the canonical three-dimension competency lattice (technical/professional/leadership) and Bloom's taxonomy; Team Capability addresses required competencies and competency levels for SE roles; Technical Leadership references competency frameworks for leadership; Enterprise Capability Management discusses organizational baseline competency.

III. Structural Read

Editorial-state observation. Dispersed-instrument pattern (eight carriers). SE-039 §VII.6 candidate.

Cluster A (universal-sibling lattice, Doc 572 Appendix D), two-axis sub-form (SE-039 §VII.6 from SE-082). Two co-located lattices stress-test the two-axis universal-sibling candidate at competency rung. Axis-1: competency dimensions (technical, professional, leadership) — SE-033 universal-sibling, three-axis. Axis-2: proficiency levels (awareness → supervised practitioner → practitioner → lead practitioner → expert, per INCOSE Competency Framework) — Doc 572 Appendix D.5 ordinal sub-form. Two-axis = dimension × level, with each cell representing a distinct assessable state. SE-082 introduced two-axis universal-sibling (stakeholder roles × lifecycle-stages); SE-157 confirms at competency rung. SE-039 §VII.6 candidate is now formalization-ready at multiple instances.

Cluster B (multi-keeper composition, Doc 604), three-scale sub-form (SE-039 §VII.6 from SE-115). Assessment occurs at three scales: individual (Assessing Individuals), team (Team Capability), enterprise (Enterprise Capability Management). SE-115's three-scale sub-form (intra-organization / inter-organization / federated) is structurally analogous: competency assessment is intra-organization (individual within team within enterprise). The three-scale sub-form gains a third instance after SE-115 Logistics and SE-152 PfM — formalization-ready.

Cluster D (co-production at sub-rungs, Doc 573). Competency assessment is co-produced: the assessor-keeper supplies the rubric (rung-2 affordance); the assessee-substrate supplies performance evidence (rung-1). Neither alone produces the competency rating.

Cluster G (SIPE, Doc 541), assessment-substrate rung instance (SE-039 §VII.6 SE-104 prior). Competency assessment is itself a structurally-insulated practice — the assessment regime carries its own coherence independent of any single assessor or assessee. SE-104 already supplied the assessment-substrate Cluster G instance; SE-157 is a second instance, confirming the rung.

Cluster K (virtue constraints, Doc 314 §9.5), V3 stress-test. Competency assessment is V3-as-procedure-binding: the discipline exists because individual judgment about "is this practitioner competent" is structurally insufficient at organizational scale; the assessment procedure binds the rating. Fifth V3 sub-mode candidate (after bias-mitigation, lifecycle-tracking, formalization-consistency, claim-binding from SE-156): rating-binding. V3-as-procedure-binding now spans five sub-modes.

Cluster H (hypostatic boundary, Doc 372). Competency describes what practitioners do; the discipline does not claim what they ARE. SE-033 already noted this; SE-157 confirms.
